original_full_abstract_TeX:
For every fixed compact convex body $K\subset\R^n$ with nonempty
interior and every real polynomial $f$, the normalized Lebesgue
sum-of-squares density bound of degree at most $2r$ has error
$O_{K,f}(r^{-2})$ for every integer $r\ge1$.
We give a self-contained proof and an explicit constant, using one
global square. A quadratic Taylor upper estimator reduces the objective
to a scalar endpoint problem. Homothetic contraction compares every
sublevel shell with the same core mass that normalizes a fixed power of
a Dirichlet polynomial; that mass cancels before summation. This proves
the quadratic upper rate in the convex-body/Lebesgue regime of the
2018 Oberwolfach question. A classical interval example shows that the
exponent is sharp in the worst case. The proxy and the broad
localization and relative-mass mechanisms have established precedents;
no firstness or new-method claim is made.

exact_claim.hierarchy: H_r=inf integral_K f q dx over globally SOS q of degree<=2r, integral_K q dx=1, r integer>=1; reference is n-dimensional Lebesgue.
exact_claim.quantifiers: For every fixed n>=1, compact convex full-dimensional K, every real polynomial f, any minimizer a in K, all r>=1. No smooth/semialgebraic boundary or convexity of f required.
exact_claim.constant: H=max_K Hessian operator norm, gamma=1+H/2, g=grad f(a).(x-a)+gamma||x-a||², G=max_K g>0, L=n+2, C_n=4L²(pi/2)^(2L)(1+2^(n+2)); 0<=H_r-f*<=C_n G/r². Single normalized global square witness.
exact_claim.sharpness: For interval [0,1], f=t, H_r>=1/[4(r+1)²]; product with [-1,1]^(n-1) same. One worst-case fixed instance in each dimension, not positive lower rate for every objective.
exact_claim.extension: Also C² objectives on open neighborhood of K using same quadratic proxy and derivative maxima.
exact_claim.exclusions: No arbitrary reference measure, lower-dimensional K with n-dimensional Lebesgue, nonconvex body, efficient minimizer-location method, objective-only-polynomial hierarchy for general nonconvex f, firstness or new-method assertion.
